text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages with eight quote variants each, for testing a citation checker.

passages.source_passage: Board members will recall that the Harrowfield Family Reunion Service expanded its foster placements in March 2023. By the end of the second quarter, 46 children were living with vetted foster families across the Kessel Valley districts, up from thirty-one in January. Caseworkers completed family tracing for 19 of these children, and twelve have since been reunified with relatives. Not every trace led to a safe outcome: in four cases, assessors found that the extended family could not provide adequate care. No child was returned to a household without a follow-up visit within 14 days. Staff turnover remains a concern, as 22 percent of caseworkers left the service during the period. The team requests that the board approve two additional supervisor posts before the next financial year.

passages.source_passage: Monitoring period: July to December 2024. The Brennick Vocational Skills Centre enrolled 240 young people aged 16 to 24 in its welding, tailoring and solar installation courses. Attendance averaged 87% across all cohorts, although the solar course recorded lower figures during the rainy season. Of the 198 trainees who completed their courses, sixty-three secured paid work within three months. Female trainees did not enrol in the welding stream in significant numbers, with only nine women joining. The centre's job placement officer visited 35 local employers to promote apprenticeships. Equipment shortages were not resolved during the period, and two of the five welding stations remained out of service. Data on graduate earnings has not yet been verified by the field team.

passages.source_passage: During 2023, the Saltmere Coastal Early Warning Programme extended its siren and SMS alert network to 14 fishing villages along the Corran estuary. With the Foundation's support, volunteers installed six new tide gauges and trained 410 household representatives in evacuation procedures. When Cyclone Imra approached in October, alerts reached an estimated 92 percent of registered households at least eighteen hours before landfall. No deaths were recorded in programme villages, although two fishermen from a neighbouring settlement were reported missing. The programme did not meet its target for disability-inclusive drills, completing only three of the planned eight. We remain grateful to the Foundation and propose to prioritise accessible shelters in the coming year.

passages.source_passage: Session 3: Before You Visit a Household. Volunteers in the Duvall Hills Borehole and Latrine Project should remember that each borehole serves around 250 people, so queues are common in the morning. Never promise a family that a new latrine will be built for them; allocations are decided by the village water committee. In the 2022 baseline, only 38% of households had a handwashing station near the latrine. Ask the household to show you where they wash hands, but do not inspect the latrine unless invited. Each visit should take no longer than twenty minutes. Record your observations on the green form and hand it to your supervisor by Friday. Remember that you are a guest, not an inspector.

passages.source_passage: This report covers the Kiremba Farmer Field School Network for the 2023 long-rains season. Facilitators ran 52 field schools, each with between twenty and thirty members, giving a total enrolment of 1,340 farmers. Demonstration plots using compost and mulching produced average maize yields 31 percent higher than comparison plots managed with conventional practice. Adoption on members' own farms was slower: monitors found that 41 percent of members had not applied compost by the end of the season. Seed fairs were held in six sub-locations, but the bean seed supplier didn't deliver on time. Facilitator refresher training, scheduled for August, was postponed to November because of budget delays.

passages.source_passage: Between 4 and 18 September 2024, the Lowmarsh Malaria Prevention Campaign distributed 61,500 long-lasting insecticidal nets across three health zones. Distribution teams used household registers compiled in June, allocating one net for every two people. At each site, community volunteers assisted the zone health officers with crowd control. Post-distribution checks in a sample of 600 households found that 79% of nets were hanging over a sleeping space. Monitors noted that nets weren't hung in many kitchens and outdoor sleeping areas used during hot weather. In Tessaly zone, the registers did not include roughly four hundred newly arrived families, who received nets only after a mop-up round in October. Pregnant women and children under five were prioritised at every site. The next survey will be conducted in March 2025.

passages.source_passage: Since the floods of 2021, demand for psychosocial support in the Orrin Basin has risen sharply. The Willowgate Community Counselling Service currently employs eleven trained lay counsellors, who held 2,860 individual sessions last year. At present, clinic nurses refer most new clients to our counsellors. A 2023 screening exercise found that 27 percent of adults attending primary clinics reported symptoms of moderate or severe distress. Yet the nearest psychiatric unit is 140 kilometres away, and there is no specialist service within the district. Many clients told us they would not seek help from a clinic because of stigma. Our lay counsellors are recruited from the communities they serve, and this proposal seeks funding to train eight more over two years.

passages.source_passage: In 2024, the Mbirani District Community Health Programme supported 318 community health workers across 47 villages. Each worker visited an average of 22 households per month, screening children for malnutrition and referring pregnant women for antenatal care. Thanks to your grant, every worker now carries a solar-charged phone with the referral app installed. Referrals completed at health facilities rose from 54% in 2023 to 71% this year. However, stipends were not paid on time in the first quarter, and some workers stopped reporting for several weeks. Supervision visits fell short of plan, with no visits at all in the two most remote villages during the rainy months. We have since agreed a new payment schedule with the district health office.

passages.source_passage: Rainfall in the Tamsin Plateau has become increasingly erratic over the past two decades. Records from the Okoro weather station show that total seasonal rainfall fell by about 18 percent between 2004 and 2023, while dry spells lengthened. Most of the plateau's 9,000 smallholder households still plant long-maturing maize, which did not survive the 2022 drought on many farms. Sorghum, millet and cowpea varieties suited to shorter seasons are known locally but are not widely grown, because certified seed is rarely available. In a pilot run by Greenfold Resilience Trust, 120 farmers who received drought-tolerant sorghum harvested twice as much grain as their neighbours. This proposal builds on that pilot.

passages.source_passage: This update summarises progress in the Calder Ridge Cash for Food Programme to 30 June 2024. A total of 3,450 households received monthly transfers of 45 dollars through mobile money, compared with a target of 3,800. Post-distribution monitoring found that 82% of recipients spent most of the transfer on food, mainly maize flour, beans and cooking oil. Market prices did not rise significantly in the four monitored markets, suggesting the transfers caused no local inflation. However, around 150 enrolled households never received their May payment because of a network outage. The finance team has reconciled all accounts, and the board is asked to approve an extension to December.
